title: Bounded publisher-reference reading across the Freedom Series
review_kind: AI-assisted publisher-reference text reading, not human or audio verification

coverage.first_episode: Full extracted-text reading already recorded separately; not resampled or overwritten here
coverage.token_definition: Unicode regex \b[\w]+(?:[’'][\w]+)?\b, no case normalization or stemming; whitespace count also provided
coverage.running_header_trigger_scope: Four of eighteen keyword-trigger windows; retained as disclosed sampling artifacts, not evidence of topic frequency
coverage.question_classification_denominator: Nine W06 trigger windows only; not a full-corpus rate

method: Six deterministic windows per additional episode: opening, two keyword windows, two question windows and the first question-bearing non-ADAMUS publisher role turn. Full rules and exact raw windows are retained privately.

episodes.title: The Voice of Freedom
episodes.interpretation: Forgiveness is explicitly linked back to the preceding session. Selected passages frame personal freedom against collective politics and describe multiple possible Earths. An audience participant answers a prompted future-of-humanity exercise; these are source interpretations and scenarios, not validated forecasts.

episodes.title: End of an Era
episodes.interpretation: A financial-bank metaphor presents spiritual energy as freely available. A pop-quiz format asks participants about near-term global changes. One participant reports bodily symptoms and offers a spiritual explanation; neither her interpretation nor the facilitator response supplies clinical evidence.

episodes.title: Beyond Your Dream (Into Freedom)
episodes.interpretation: Sovereignty is performed as a personal declaration and discussed in relation to learned limitations. The facilitator urges releasing old dreams and attributes wider life difficulties to unavailable dreams. The sample shows this causal framing, not evidence that releasing dreams changes health or finances.

episodes.title: The Dream of the Soul
episodes.interpretation: The sample connects abundance with an enacted attitude and presents the soul’s dream as embodied clarity. It explicitly distinguishes crystalline clarity from physical stones in one passage, while a later guided passage makes unverified ageless-body and symptom-relief claims.

episodes.title: Illuminated Dreams
episodes.interpretation: The opening presents Adamus, St. Germain and a divine self-name as facets of the narrated identity. Other samples develop psychic gravity, inward knowing and portals associated with desired experiences. Imagined self-questions about readiness are not audience submissions.

episodes.title: It Comes to You
episodes.interpretation: The session explicitly uses an entertainment/game-show format, with a mock announcer audition and audience voting. Abundance and self-sovereignty are linked in the facilitator’s criticism of reliance on help. A separate passage describes crystal-filled caves as energy mechanisms; no physical verification is provided.

episodes.title: Bringers of the New Energy
episodes.interpretation: The opening distinguishes this meeting from the preceding entertainment session. Selected teaching passages define consciousness through self-existence, contrast passion and inward knowing with mental control, and introduce an energy-focused experiential exercise. These are spiritual constructs without operational physical measurements.

episodes.title: How to Live
episodes.interpretation: The sample interprets events in Egypt through a spiritual freedom framework, then turns to participants’ experiences of self-acceptance, social approval and embodiment. A guided exercise urges assuming enlightenment without qualifying objections. This does not establish a geopolitical explanation or an observed therapeutic outcome.

episodes.title: Expectations of Enlightenment
episodes.interpretation: Participants are prompted to describe expectations of enlightenment, including ease and greater understanding. One participant says life has not become easy; the facilitator reframes the expectation. Relationships are discussed through self-love and external obligations, providing a point for comparing promises with reported difficulty.

themes.paraphrase: Selected passages repeatedly place authority in the self, including sovereignty declarations, embodied clarity and self-acceptance.
Energy language supports accounts of abundance, consciousness and desired experience; its meaning ranges from metaphor to claimed mechanisms.
The samples contrast letting go of old dreams and anticipating ease with participants reporting uncertainty or difficulty.
Quizzes, demonstrations, game-show voting, banter and guided exercises structure participation. Publisher stage directions describe the format but are not acoustic measurements.
Samples discuss elections, near-term changes and Egypt within the contemporary spiritual narrative. Source dates remain in 2012–2013; this is not a current prediction feed.
Some passages link bodily experience or relief to spiritual transformation. Participant testimony and facilitator assertions remain unverified and are not medical evidence.
Selected passages frame personal development against perceived obligations, outside approval or dependence on others. This is a recurrent narrative tension, not a tested causal account.

question_window_classifications.rationale: The participant repeats a future-oriented question while responding to the facilitator; the window continues as an elicited exercise.
The selected question requests a scribe; the broader passage introduces a pop quiz.
The selected question teases the promised short meeting and a football game.
Coffee and sweetness banter is mixed with hosting logistics.
The selected question concerns placement of the drawing board.
The participant responds during an explicitly staged announcer audition; this is not a substantive advice question.
The question follows playful comments about a Superman figurine.
A participant uses a question-shaped self-description while answering the facilitator’s attitude prompt.
The selected reaction and later age song concern the persona’s claimed birthday.

limits: One publisher and one human medium; not a cross-medium or biological-ET comparison.
Episode 1 has full extracted-text reading; episodes 2–10 only six fixed windows each. No claim of complete ten-episode reading.
Keyword/question selection is deterministic but enriched, not representative or randomized; temporal and thematic prevalence cannot be inferred.
Running headers remain in extraction and can trigger freedom keyword selection; headers and stage annotations must be removed before lexical frequency comparisons.
Questions can be logistics, humor, imagined dialogue, self-questioning or facilitator prompts. A question mark alone does not establish genuine audience Q&A.
The role locator recognizes a bounded capitalized-label pattern; labels with additional parenthetical formatting may be missed. It is not a complete role parser.
Short windows can truncate turns and answers; no unseen answer is reconstructed.
Publisher roles and stage directions are documentary labels, not independently verified voices or audio events.
Spiritual, medical, financial and historical assertions are attributed source claims; no external truth or causality validation is performed.
PDF extraction order and line-break artifacts may affect windows and token counts; exact text and source hashes are retained.
Codebook and interpretive themes were formulated after these windows were read; they are exploratory, not preregistered or independently double-coded.

hypotheses.statement: Performed sessions may yield more question marks and audience-response annotations than lecture passages.
hypotheses.required_test: Type questions by role and function over complete texts; compare matched-length passages and report annotator agreement. Do not treat publisher annotations as measured audio events.

hypotheses.statement: Shared energy/crystal vocabulary may connect semantically different claims in naive topic networks.
hypotheses.required_test: Code contextual senses, including metaphorical clarity, spiritual resources and claimed material mechanisms; compare contextual clustering with TF-IDF after header removal.

hypotheses.statement: Self-responsibility language may co-occur with money, body and relationship concerns.
hypotheses.required_test: Apply a fixed codebook to complete passages, separate participant self-report from facilitator causal attribution, and compare within-source baselines.

hypotheses.statement: The narrative framing around late 2012 may shift from anticipation toward retrospective integration.
hypotheses.required_test: Review complete dated passages with a fixed chronology and explicit prediction targets; verify historical events separately. This sample cannot establish forecast accuracy.
